yarn-dinkum.meaning: Every instruction kept, including the repeated noise warning, the pack, sideways retreat, "Bears can run as fast as a racehorse, uphill and down", and the brown/black bear split: "leave your pack on and PLAY DEAD" vs "DO NOT PLAY DEAD". Nothing added.
yarn-dinkum.sense: Terms fit: "Once a bear's clocked you" (noticed), "Pick up any littlies straight away", "If it gets your tucker", "Bushwalk and get about in groups". "if she reckons you're a danger to her cubs" softens 'perceives' to 'thinks' but still works.
yarn-dinkum.authenticity: Sounds like an Australian ranger's plain-spoken notice: "Mind you, check the advice for each park you visit", "wait till the bear moves off", "anything you can lay your hands on".
yarn-dinkum.register: A light touch suited to level 2: "clocked", "littlies", "Bushwalk", "tucker", "heaps", "reckons", "till", in clear plain English. No swearing.
yarn-dinkum.tone: Stays a calm, serious safety notice; caps kept: "Do NOT run or make any sudden movements." and "do NOT play dead—fight back!"
yarn-dinkum.flow: Reads smoothly: "If the bear's not moving, back away slowly and sideways; that way you can keep an eye on it and you won't trip over." One clunky phrase: "being ready for it in your head".
yarn-dinkum.variety: Good spread, "tucker" twice (as in the original's 'food' twice): "clocked", "littlies", "Bushwalk", "tucker", "heaps", "put a bear off".
yarn-dinkum.essence: Unmistakably the park service's bear guidance, same structure and headings: "Brown/Grizzly Bears:", "Black Bears:", "Bear Attacks".

yarn-deadset.meaning: Complete and close to the original: "a few more strategies can help stop the situation getting worse", "Lie flat on your stomach", "try to fight back with any object you can find".
yarn-deadset.sense: "Pick up littlies straight away", "Getting your tucker", "Bushwalk and travel in groups", "go up heaps" fit. "Let the bear know who you are" is a little off: the point is what you are (a human), not who.
yarn-deadset.authenticity: Natural plain Australian English: "Stay still; stand your ground but slowly wave your arms.", "wait until the bear moves off". Some original phrasing kept: "Moving sideways is also non-threatening to bears."
yarn-deadset.register: Light, a little lighter than A: "littlies", "Bushwalk", "tucker", "heaps", "behaviour". Right at level 2's light touch.
yarn-deadset.tone: Calm and serious: "Do NOT run or make any sudden movements." and "Above all, keep your distance from bears!"
yarn-deadset.flow: Clean, if a bit stiff in kept lines: "So bears often pick up on groups of people from further away, and because of their combined size, groups also put bears off."
yarn-deadset.essence: The original guidance intact, with headings and caps: "PLAY DEAD", "DO NOT PLAY DEAD".

yarn-troppo.meaning: All instructions survive, but it adds claims: "Grizzlies and black bears can both climb trees, and better than you.", "That's a bear telling you to give it some room.", "so you've got no hope of outrunning it", "you won't go head over heels on a tree root". Most elaborate the original; "and better than you" is a new claim.
yarn-troppo.sense: Mostly fits: "so it twigs you're a human", "a bear standing up is usually just having a stickybeak", "their patch", "a feed of your tucker". "it's armour for your back" overstates 'can provide protection'.
yarn-troppo.authenticity: Rich and mostly natural: "Not lunch.", "same as you", "wait till the bear wanders off", "every poor soul coming down the track after you". The opener "Listen up, cos this is the stuff that keeps you in one piece." is a little performed.
yarn-troppo.register: Well heavier than level 2: an added spoken opener, asides "(anyone who's shared a tent after a week on the track knows it)", "like a crab", "you do not want to be on the wrong end of that". No swearing.
yarn-troppo.tone: Still treats the danger seriously and keeps the caps, but the jokes lighten a safety notice: "Not lunch.", "(anyone who's shared a tent after a week on the track knows it)", "like a crab".
yarn-troppo.flow: Lively and readable, the repeat warning handled neatly: "And again, cos it matters: don't make any loud noises or screams". Some asides interrupt the instructions.
yarn-troppo.variety: Widely varied: "clocked", "twigs", "stickybeak", "mob of people", "a feed of your tucker", "head over heels", "patch", "getting your head right". "cos" twice, "And" openers recur.
yarn-troppo.essence: Recognisably the bear guidance with its structure, but recast as a ranger's yarn; the official notice's character is partly lost: "Listen up, cos this is the stuff that keeps you in one piece."

engine.meaning: The original nearly word for word, so every point is kept: "additional strategies can help prevent the situation from escalating".
engine.sense: "Getting your tucker" fits. "Pick up little fellas immediately" is off: 'little fellas' is a pet name for boys or a mate's kid, not the general 'small children' of a warning.
engine.authenticity: The few swaps sit in unchanged formal American prose, making odd joins: "prevent a bear from accessing your tucker", "Pick up little fellas immediately.", and leaves "Lay ﬂat on your stomach".
engine.register: Largely untranslated: apart from "behaviour", "recognise", "little fellas" and "tucker", it is the original: "However, please check recommendations for each park you visit".
engine.tone: Being the original, the serious tone survives: "Do NOT run or make any sudden movements."
engine.flow: Reads as the original, except the jarring slang-in-formal joins: "prevent a bear from accessing your tucker".
engine.variety: Too few terms to vary: "little fellas", "tucker" twice.
engine.essence: Unmistakably the original, being almost the original.

unharnessed.meaning: All points kept: "a few extra tricks can help stop things getting worse", "keep your pack on and PLAY DEAD", "try to fight back with any object you can get hold of". "not something to eat" renders 'not a prey animal' faithfully.
unharnessed.sense: "Getting your tucker", "Clear out of the area", "flip you over" fit. "most bears don't want to have a go at you" works (attack). "Let the bear know who you are" has the same slight slip as 'who' for 'what'.
unharnessed.authenticity: Natural plain Australian English: "Bears might bluff their way out of an encounter by charging and then pulling away at the last second." Nothing forced.
unharnessed.register: On the light side of level 2: mostly plain English with "tucker", "have a go at you", "Clear out", keeping "Hike and travel in groups" where others say bushwalk.
unharnessed.tone: Calm and serious throughout: "Do NOT climb a tree.", "Above all, keep your distance from bears!"
unharnessed.flow: Smooth: "If the bear isn't moving, back off slowly and sideways; that way you can keep an eye on the bear and not trip over."
unharnessed.variety: Few terms but no tic: "tucker", "have a go at you", "Clear out", "flip".
unharnessed.essence: The guidance intact, structure and caps kept: "Brown/Grizzly Bears:", "DO NOT PLAY DEAD".

yarn-dinkum.quote: being ready for it in your head
yarn-dinkum.why: A slightly awkward rendering of a plain phrase.

yarn-troppo.original: Groups of people are usually noisier and smellier than a single person.

yarn-troppo.original: Both grizzlies and black bears can climb trees.

yarn-troppo.original: it can provide protection for your back
yarn-troppo.why: Overstates the protection a pack gives; a safety-relevant exaggeration.

summaries.yarn-dinkum: Accurate, clear and lightly Aussie; the best fit for a level-2 safety notice.
summaries.yarn-deadset: Faithful and clear with a light Aussie touch; a hair stiffer than A.
summaries.yarn-troppo: Vivid and mostly authentic, but too heavy for level 2 and jokier than a safety notice should be.
summaries.engine: Barely touched: a couple of word swaps that sit awkwardly in the original's formal prose.
summaries.unharnessed: Clear, natural and accurate, a shade light for level 2.
